chunks: And with this chain, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn 'Uqba, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, from Hamran, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'For that reason did We prescribe to the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely.'
He (peace be upon him) replied: 'He will be placed in a place in Hell to which the severity of the punishment of its people reaches; if he killed all people, he would only enter that place.'
I said: 'And if he kills another?' He replied: 'His punishment is doubled.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for murder according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) in relation to the Quranic verse?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphorical weight of the verse in Surah Al-Ma'idah, clarifying that the 'killing of all mankind' refers to the magnitude of the sin rather than a literal count, establishing a specific locus of punishment in Hell. He further distinguishes between the initial severity and the compounding nature of the penalty, noting that while the location remains fixed, the intensity of the torment is doubled for each additional life taken, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on both the qualitative gravity and quantitative escalation of bloodshed.
